dhp33:1: Thoughts, unsteady, fickle, difficult to guard, difficult to control,
dhp33:3: A wise man makes straight, even as a fletcher his arrow.
dhp34:1: Like a fish thrown up on dry land from his watery home.
dhp34:3: These thoughts writhe and quiver in their efforts to shake off the power of Māra.
dhp35:1: Thoughts are unruly and flighty, and flit and flutter wherever they list.
dhp35:3: It is a good thing to tame the thoughts; tamed thoughts bring happiness.
dhp36:1: Thoughts are exceedingly hard to see, exceedingly subtle, and flit and flutter wherever they list.
dhp36:3: A wise man should guard his thoughts; guarded thoughts bring happiness.
dhp37:1: Thoughts wander afar, wander alone, are bodiless, seek a hiding place;
dhp37:3: Whoso restrain their thoughts will obtain release from the bond of Māra.
dhp38:1: He whose heart abides not steadfast.
dhp38:2: He who knows not the Good Law,
dhp38:4: Such a man lacks perfect wisdom.
dhp39:1: He whose heart is unwetted by the rain of lust.
dhp39:2: He whose heart is unsinged by the fire of ill-will.
dhp39:3: He who has renounced both good and evil.
dhp39:4: He who is vigilant, - such a man has nothing to fear.
dhp40:1: Realizing that this body is fragile as a jar, establishing these thoughts as firm as a city,
dhp40:3: One should attack Māra with the weapon of wisdom; one should stand guard over Māra when he is defeated; one should never rest.
dhp41:1: In no long time this body will lie on the ground,
dhp41:3: Despised, with consciousness departed, like a useless log.
dhp42:1: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy,
dhp42:3: Thoughts attached to falsehood will do a man yet more harm.
dhp43:1: Neither mother nor father could do this, nor other relatives besides;
dhp43:3: Thoughts well-directed could do this far better.
